content.v: 近日Jagex宣布，《符文之境：重燃》计划于12月2日上线。所有重燃角色将从3级起步，并采用全新经济体系。这项内容希望让新玩家和一段时间没有游玩的老玩家，从共同起点进入已有25年历史的游戏世界。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261004/1791062817_546320_jpg_r.jpg
Jagex此前在RuneFest 2026公布了《符文之境：重燃》，随后于10月3日进一步说明调整方向。重燃角色会与其他玩家处于同一个世界，共同活动；现有玩家无需放弃原来的游玩方式。
预告片介绍的规则还包括不设置“寻宝者”和付费进度。Jagex表示，这次调整重视进度、挑战、社区和有意义的奖励，希望改善新玩家不知从何开始、老玩家回归时难以跟上变化的问题。
《符文之境：重燃》上线后，重燃角色在前10天可免费访问会员内容。

Finals 1 & Finals 2 of PEC: Fall is the final chance for teams to earn PGC Points, which they will use to qualify to the PUBG Global Championship (PGC) 2026, in Istanbul, Türkiye! The PGC Points slot will then be assigned to the next best ranked EMEA team in the PGC Points standings. If more than one Turkish team qualify for PGC via PGC Points directly, the top-ranked team will receive the Host Team Wildcard.

Even if a PEC: Fall tournament title or ticket to Istanbul isn’t in your future, you can still tune in and earn Drops by watching the broadcast live on Twitch and Kick! https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261004/1791062586_103473.png

content.v: 《战争机器：事变日》目前获得86分评价，成为一篇Xbox策略评论讨论主机独占的近期案例。外媒Comicbook编辑认为，本作初期评价让Xbox选择主机独占显得更有吸引力，但独占策略的效果仍需等游戏上市后观察。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261004/1791060988_251872_jpg_r.jpg
编辑回忆称，自己当年为了玩《战争机器2》购买了Xbox360，并由此提出一个问题：独占游戏如今能否再次为Xbox主机提供清晰的购买理由。据评论所述，《战争机器：事变日》目前的评分是系列自《战争机器3》以来最高的，不过随着评价数量增加，分数仍可能变化。
《战争机器：事变日》将故事带回马库斯·菲尼克斯与多姆·圣地亚哥 对抗 兽族的早期阶段。本作将于10月6日发售，编辑认为上市后的表现才是进一步观察这一策略效果的节点。
评论还将《发条革命》视为下一项重要检验，并提到《神鬼寓言4》采取多平台发行安排。编辑并不主张Xbox所有游戏都独占：多人游戏和持续运营游戏可能受益于更大的跨平台玩家群体，而有说服力的单人独占作品则可能帮助主机建立辨识度。

content.v: 近日PlayStation社区用户RealRadec发文称自己的PSN账号遭到入侵。他表示自己多次尝试登录并修改密码，登出所有设备，还重新启用了双重验证，但账号原本关联的邮箱仍被更改。这起自述事件再次引发社区对PSN账号安全的关注。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261004/1791060939_257901_jpg_r.jpg
RealRadec在X上拥有超过3万名关注者。今年早些时候，多名PlayStation玩家卷入社交工程相关争议；播客主持人Colin Moriarty的账号遭劫持后，相关问题曾受到广泛讨论。他后来借助自身人脉重新取得账号访问权。
此前讨论的一种账号劫持方式，可能利用PSN用户名、关联邮箱，以及交易编号或购买日期等信息。部分信息可能公开可见，另一些则可能被推断出来。不过，目前没有证据表明RealRadec此次遭遇采用了同一种方法。
数字购买内容和奖杯记录的积累，也让玩家担心失去账号后会一并失去购买内容与使用记录。RealRadec此次账号异常的具体原因，以及账号是否已经恢复，仍有待确认。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

content.v: 近日外媒PushSquare就2026年10月PS Plus基本档游戏阵容发起读者投票，并在文章中讨论三款游戏的吸引力。作者认为本月阵容缺少能吸引订阅者的作品。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261004/1791060697_748886_jpg_r.jpg
《F1 25》被当作主打游戏，这是一款扎实的赛车模拟游戏，本身素质不错，F1爱好者值得一试，但放在十月这个恐怖主题月份，缺少话题爆点。
《猎杀：对决1896》是一款多人撤离射击游戏，游戏口碑积淀接近十年，压抑阴森氛围极具特色，但多人撤离射击的类型门槛，会劝退一部分订阅用户，适合约好友一起游玩。
《地球防卫军：方块世界2》是体素风格的地球防卫军衍生作品。保留系列疯狂热闹的战斗特色，战役模式对抗海量外星入侵者。本作同样不是面向全部玩家，编辑推荐大家尝试，联机合作游玩欢乐效果更佳。
页面所载投票结果显示，在166张满意度投票中，63%的受访者选择最负面的选项。另一项有152人参与的投票中，72%表示没有特别期待的游戏。评论区也出现不同意见：有人觉得阵容过于小众，也有人认为订阅服务正适合尝试平时不会单独购买的作品。

items.title: 《战争机器：E-Day》开发者“自豪地成为 Xbox 的主要游戏之一”，并重新关注独占性
items.summary: The Gears of War: E-Day developers at The Coalition say they are "proud to be one of Xbox's main titles" as Mi

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/01/btfiuoeldu6mkzuez7e008xhvd1icgg-jcb-u5aiuoy-1790813782471.jpeg
The Gears of War: E-Day developers at The Coalition say they are "proud to be one of Xbox's main titles" as Microsoft refocuses on exclusivity.

Studio art director Aryan Hanbeck and creative director Matt Searcy opened up about The Coalition's place in the Xbox portfolio during an interview with gaming news content creator Destin Lergarie (via MP1st ). Searcy said he and the rest of the team were "proud" when asked how they feel about Gears of War: E-Day's status as an Xbox exclusive.

"Well, we feel great because Gears has such a long, storied… It's part of Xbox's DNA. It's woven into it," he said. "At The Coalition, we feel pretty honored to have Gears and be the ones bringing that legacy forward. We know how much it means to people. We know how much it means to us."

Gears of War: E-Day is firmly a console exclusive, but there was a lot of confusion surrounding which platforms Gears of War: E-Day would be available on as recently as four months ago. The once-Xbox-exclusive franchise made its debut on PlayStation consoles when original remaster, Gears of War: Reloaded, released in August 2025. Many took its presence on PS5 as a sign not only that the series would continue to come to Sony's console but also that the days of exclusive titles may nearly be behind us – and for a while, that seemed to be the case.

Leaked listings and rumors were officially shut down at the Xbox Games Showcase 2026 when Xbox CEO Asha Sharma proudly declared that Marcus Fenix and Dom Santiago's Emergence Day prequel story would only be coming to Xbox Series X/S and PC . It was a shock decision that arrived as the Microsoft gaming entity kicked off a broader push for more exclusive games . Perhaps even more shocking at the time were the announcements that immediately followed, including the company's promise to never release Xbox exclusive titles on rival platforms .

After leaked splash art fanned rumors that Xbox hastily decided to cancel a Gears of War: E-Day PS5 port, the company said it did not make any "last-minute" decisions when it comes to its platform choice. While Searcy said it brought The Coalition joy to see their new game leading Microsoft's renewed interest in exclusive titles, making sure they made a great game was what came first.

"I think this is true of most game devs: You're just passionate about your craft," he said. "We're all gamers first and foremost. We love making games. We love making Gears. So, from our perspective, we just wanted to make the best goddamn Gears game we could. We wanted it to be a technical and art showpiece, and I think getting to see Asha on-stage say, 'To return to Xbox, we're returning to Gears,' yeah, that's a really cool moment.

He continued: "We know how much Xbox means to a lot of people. We're proud to be one of Xbox's main titles – I think it's been that way for a long time – and it's pretty cool to show up now and fill that role again."

Gears of War: E-Day launched in early access for Premium Edition players on PC and Xbox Series X/S October 1, 2026. Its full launch will follow this week, October 6. IGN's early review, which covered only the campaign mode, returned a 9/10 . The game's story director was laid off just one week before it made its way to players' hands a few days ago. Now, more developers at The Coalition is bracing for additional layoffs .

Wallhacks have plagued Call of Duty for years, but in Modern Warfare 4 , Activision has a plan to change that.

If you're unfamiliar with the term, wallhacks are a type of cheat that allows nefarious players to see their opponents' every move through walls. Call of Duty is far from the only multiplayer-centric gaming franchise to suffer from cheaters who use the tool, but it might be the most infamous example – and in Modern Warfare 4, that's all about to change.

As detailed in a new video published on the franchise's official social media pages, publisher Activision and developer Infinity Ward revealed a new system aimed at combating wallhack cheaters. Called "server culling," the goal is to make Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 more reliable – and fair – than ever before.

Few things ruin a great match faster than wondering whether an opponent earned the win or saw you through a wall. Wallhacks give cheaters information they were never meant to have. With Modern Warfare 4, we’re introducing a new way to fight back: Server Culling. Here’s how it… pic.twitter.com/62m41zMbLa

The relatively in-depth explanation touches on how cheaters have been able to use wallhacks thus far. Usually, servers share information, such as a player's in-game location, between game clients. It means that, even when you can't see an enemy hiding behind cover, waiting to pop out for an easy kill, the game itself still recognizes that the player is there.

Server culling, which saw Infinity Ward build occlusion layers into Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's environments, essentially limits information to what the player is able to see. So, if you can't see someone behind the wall, the backend can't either – and that goes for wallhackers, too.
"For legitimate players, the match plays exactly as intended," Activision explained. "For cheat developers, this creates a major new obstacle."

Server culling will touch every multiplayer map available in Modern Warfare 4 when launch arrives, but it doesn't stop there. Call of Duty's new take on DMZ, the Combat Outpost mode, Warzone, and future updates will benefit from this attack on wallhacks, too. All of this new tech works alongside pre-existing anti-cheat methods across all platforms , too.

Activision said it expects server culling to "disturb the cheat marketplace," but it won't "sit on our hands" when it comes to improving the overall experience going forward. There are plenty of different ways for cheaters to disrupt the experience for the average player, and while cheat manufacterers will no doubt look for new ways to learn from Activision's advancements, the publisher said it will do its best to stay on top of the issue.

"Cheat software can’t reveal information it never receives," the Call of Duty team explained in a follow-up post . "When a player shouldn’t be able to know where an opponent is, the server can now withhold that opponent’s location data from their hardware. It’s a new layer in the fight for fair play, working alongside the rest of our anti-cheat systems Server Culling will cover every map available at launch for MW4."
See you at launch, we'll keep at it

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S October 23, 2026. How fans will rank it amongst other installments in the franchise remains to be seen, but with changes to 2XP tokens and a villain played by Death Stranding and Casino Royale actor Mads Mikkelsen , it's clear the developers have put in the work to get players interested.
For more, you can read up on how the series' anti-cheat boss pushed back on some cheating myths . You can also check out how much Activision estimated the cheating market generates per year .

content.v: It's hard to believe it's been over a decade since The Witcher 3 first released, and even harder to believe they found a way to make Geralt's tub transformation even shinier . The seminal open world RPG's hotly anticipated remaster has finally arrived, and it's pulling people back into the Continent all these years later (now more than ever on Steam, according to SteamDB ).

The new screaming high is a whopping 123,359, which it just reached an hour ago as I write this. It's settling down now, but still pretty impressive given that its peak in August was just over 30,000. The game might be getting on in years, but it's still one of the best in its genre.

When PC Gamer's Shaun Prescott first reviewed it in 2015 , he scored the game a mighty 92% and called it "a big, beautiful, sprawling action RPG full of rich stories, and suffused with an oppressive darkness."

It may not have been a huge stride forward for the style, instead feeling like innumerable tiny steps: a bar-setting journey through Andrzej Sapkowski's setting with all the graceful execution of an Olympic gold medalist's platform dive. "The Witcher 3 doesn’t bring much that’s bracingly new to the modern RPG. It’s a series of refinements," he wrote.

It probably helps that the remaster is free if you already own the base game, which has been a Steam sale mainstay since it released to all that universal acclaim. Even with all the new bells and whistles, it's half-off as we speak for Steam's autumn sale . If you want to dive in for the first time or start a new playthrough you'll definitely finish, check out all the mods which have gotten compatibility upgrades or read our guide on how to improve Geralt's fashion sense .

items.title: 忘记 PC 玩家所说的话：《巫师 3》将永远是我的 2015 年 GOTY
items.summary: And now it looks better than ever.

content.v: Welcome to Play This Right Now, the site version of our weekly newsletter in which we celebrate a new game, update, or DLC that we think is well worth checking out. You can subscribe to the newsletter at the link if you want to get our thoughts about a new videogame happening direct to your inbox every Thursday.

The past is a foreign country, and they do things differently there. At least, this is how I explain PC Gamer of yore's selection of Metal Gear Solid 5 for Game of the Year 2015 . Meaning no offence to MGS5—a game I spent several hundred hours obtaining every achievement in, just to have an excuse to play more—speaking personally? Nothing's knocking The Witcher 3 off the pedestal of 2015's greatest triumph.

And now CDPR has gone over the whole thing with a fine brush, tweaking and enhancing it to second-quarter-of-the-21st-century fidelity. You might say, 'Didn't that happen several years ago?' Poor reader, that was merely a " next-gen update ." Now is the time of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered.

There is already discourse, to no one's great surprise. Are the graphical enhancements good? Are they bad? Do they wrench The Witcher 3's beating aesthetic heart from its chest and stomp it into the dirt? I'm not exaggerating; people really are talking like this. Ignore them. It looks excellent. In the course of play I've found myself stopping regularly just to survey a sunset skybox, or the way tender motes of light slip through Geralt's beard. Actually, I've not been doing that second one. Don't put in the article that I'm doing the second one.

There is a way in which certain game worlds become home. They become actual spaces, fixed in your mind like places from your past. That's The Witcher 3 to me: its battlefields; its main city; and clean, icy Skellige, which arrives towards the game's end like a therapy session after it has spent tens of hours oppressing you with the first two regions. Going back feels like, well, going back—walking streets that were yours as someone younger, looking at nondescript corners and patches of pavement and remembering the specific, personal myths and legends that played out there in now-dead ages.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/aNNpuJvJf2euZF2XasqEGA-1920-80.png

And it looks excellent, of course. Better than it did before, which means just as good as you remember it. So not only is The Witcher 3 Remastered like going home, it's like going home and finding someone has, in your absence, been in and aired the place out, run a duster around, and reupholstered the furniture. There are some lovely little additions too—minor new features and mechanics to smooth your way through the world.

You can, for instance, now see all your myriad quest objectives on the world map, and you can flip between focused quests (and objectives) right there with a squeeze of a gamepad trigger. The HUD is less cluttered, and a new loot feed tells you what stuff you've picked up or been given, which is rather nice for the myriad quests that end with someone telling you 'Here, take this,' without ever telling you what 'this' is.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/phNXMUhWEgvsz5sEa2nx7A-1920-80.png

There have been changes to the game's combat, too. Some fiddling to sand down some of the old jank. This may be very noticeable to some people, but I confess it's not to me. If, 11 years ago, you fired up The Witcher 3 and bounced off in revulsion at how its swordplay and sign-slinging felt, I don't think you're going to experience a sudden conversion here. That's no bad thing. I'd be upset if The Witcher 3 no longer felt like The Witcher 3, but I do wonder if CDPR was perhaps overegging the pudding with its stated goal of making the game feel, mechanically, like it released in 2026 .

The Witcher 3 Remastered is a lovely little present and, with a brand-new expansion called Songs of the Past currently pencilled in to arrive some time in 2027, an excellent excuse, especially now both of the other expansions are free.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/R2hLaPUjzDWsoHLAYjG3BA-1920-80.png
Obviously, I need to generate a new, 100%-complete save to take into the new DLC. And hey, I obviously need to see every inch of the game's newly remastered world.
What an autumn treat: a series of warm, placid nights await me, curled up on a sofa and making my way through Geralt's Big Adventure again. It's like 2015 never really went away.

items.summary: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Naoki Hamaguchi said he did his best to fight for a disc release as the industry he

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/03/final-fantasy-7-revelation-disc-1791044273575.jpg
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Naoki Hamaguchi said he did his best to fight for a disc release as the industry heads toward a "future where physical media is essentially disc-less."

The lead developer in charge of next year's new remake chapter opened up about the state of gaming during an interview with Radio Times . It's a topic he's touched on before, but this time, he explained how his own appreciation for physical media led him to push for Final Fantasy 7 Revelation to get at least one disc as the industry speeds toward an all-digital future.

"Personally, obviously, I bought lots of physical editions of games as a child. Sometimes I buy digital editions of games, but if I'm particularly attached to a title, I want to get the physical version," Hamaguchi said, noting how the topic of a fully digital future has become "particularly sensitive" in recent months. "And you know, being in the industry, sometimes I want to get my friends or acquaintances who've worked on something to sign a copy of their own game."

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is confirmed to have a disc option when it launches in 2027, but there are some caveats. When physical owners on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, for example, pop their discs in, they should know the full experience will require an additional download – and a hefty one at that . It's a decision that has some fans split, but not one Hamaguchi and the team at Square Enix took lightly .
"I do really like and appreciate physical media," he said. "I see a lot of people on social media saying, 'No disc, no purchase,' and I understand where they're coming from."

Hamaguchi acknowledged that Final Fantasy 7 Revelation does have a disc alternative for those who want it, even if it's just a "key disc" that only has "the opening." He added that he understands that "there are people out there with a lot of opinions" about the future of physical media and shared a message to those who feel most passionately about the issue.

"First of all, I've got people saying to me on social media, 'Give us a full disc version!' And so, from an overall perspective, let me first say that as the director, it's my responsibility to look after the content of the game to make sure it's fun, really exciting," he said. Then, smiling, he added, "The product line-up, the SKUs (stock keeping units), how it's going on sale; that is the responsibility of the publishing team. So, my authority there is somewhat limited."

Despite the "pressure" for disc-less editions and digital editions, Hamaguchi said he "used my position to put forth an argument for the physical version as much as possible." That resulted in negotiations, "both internally and with first parties," leading to Final Fantasy 7 Revelation's one-disc strategy. He added, "I completely understand there are those out there who may not really agree with that direction or approve of that direction," but it's what he fought for, and it's the best result he could conjure.

"I completely understand there are those out there who may not really agree with that direction or approve of that direction," he said. "But I would just say that I hope you understand that I completely see where you're coming from, and that I did my best."
He added with a laugh, "It is a very tricky subject."

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will release with a disc when it releases for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S April 8, 2027. Although its launch strategy hasn't pleased everyone, it's a date that will see it arrive months before PlayStation phases out physical releases for new PS5 games . Even after Rockstar signaled changing times when it announced a disc-less release for Grand Theft Auto 6 , Sony's decision sent shockwaves through the industry.

Gaming fans have expected an all-digital future to arrive at some point, but it seems to be here sooner than most expected. Elsewhere in the interview, Hamaguchi said he thinks "physical media will remain in some form going forward," but it's impossible to deny that change is coming.
"But the PC market, for example, is going from strength to strength, and lots of people already purchase digital copies of games and just download them.

"So, I can see a world in the not-too-distant future where physical media is essentially disc-less. You would have a copy of the code on a piece of paper inside the physical box or something like that."

For more on why the Square Enix team chose to approach Final Fantasy 7 Revelation's physical release the way it did, you can see Hamaguchi's explanation here . You can also read more about the director's love for physical media .

items.title: Deadlock是MOBA角色设计之王，这一切都归功于Valve对纽约风情的拥抱
items.summary: I want to be a part of it…

content.v: The Cursed Apple, wherein Valve’s latest MOBA Deadlock takes place, is ‘an urban fantasy setting’ in the same way that Limp Bizkit is ‘an American rock band.’ Sure, the label is accurate, but Deadlock is unmistakably, crucially, and specifically New York the same way Fred Durst is sort of like the living avatar of Jacksonville, Florida.

The latest batch of new heroes just unveiled as part of the City Never Sleeps embraces this aspect of the game and takes it to new heights. Almost all the new characters are the sights and sounds of New York City: old man playing chess in the park? That’s Solomon, a chessboard-wielding wizard. A grandma on a park bench, feeding pigeons? That’s Baba, a cheeky twist on Slavic folklore. What about those giant, slimy rats always gnawing on floor pizza? Enter the literal Rat King, who makes all of da rules.

Just look at this fan concept for a Chinese immigrant and construction worker reimagined as Sun Wukong (who natural law mandates must appear as a playable character in every MOBA ). Deadlock’s online community is always abuzz with ruminations about what comes next the same way you can find with games like Heroes of the Storm or Smash Bros., but their enthusiasm isn’t for games they’ve already played or stories that have already been told. It’s for the winding alleyways and wild card denizens of the real-life NYC, pulled through a prism of macabre magic.

Maybe that sounds like a gimmick, but the game is never content to leave these characters without dimension. Vyper isn’t just a slithering sewer lizard with a firearm, she’s a chronic flirt and a dismal career criminal. Seven may be a cackling pulp serial villain, but mark his tender memories of friendly wight Kelvin and his affinity for the naive, almost childlike goo monster Viscous.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/58ZH7CWxxXKpZpcjbHRnT8-1920-80.jpg

It's refreshing because a lot of MOBA heroes are basically action figures: emphatic, unsubtle, function-first designs where narrative is a secondary priority at best. It’s obvious why this is if you know the genre’s history—MOBA progenitor DotA's designs all came from Warcraft, and its successors haven't been able to fully get away from that. Sure, Dota 2’s Disruptor has a unique backstory, and he’s an oglodi rather than an orc , but no amount of reverse-engineering will erase the truth from my memory: he is Thrall, but red.

League isn't too far off from that, taking generic character concepts with rough DotA counterparts and retooling them for a standalone game—one with a narrative that wouldn’t be figured out for years. Heroes of the Storm's Smash Bros. grab bag of Blizzard favorites has its own charm, but it certainly isn't cohesive. Smite draws from a different well, but real-world mythology is even more archetypal and constrained by prior assumptions than Blizzard's fantasy cast.

That’s not to say you can’t tell a good story with ‘Thrall, but red.' Dota 2 actually has a lot of fun storytelling if you look for it. But Deadlock breaks new ground for MOBA-pilled lore fiends simply because it's not so beholden to its forebears.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/jE5RZDnhpGR6GUWE7qQ4V8-1920-80.jpg

Deadlock is the rare MOBA with both an original story to tell and the blank canvas necessary to tell it best. Valve has seized this opportunity with apparent relish, and you can see the results of that in the oodles of fan art pouring out for each of the newest six characters, only one of whom is even out at this point. Every time the community gets its hands on unique names for over 100 of the Rat King's unique rat citizens or Valve patches in " over 10,000 non-ping voice lines " in a single pre-release update, playtest enthusiasm renews all over again (it just hit a new all-time concurrent player count peak yesterday, according to SteamDB ).
CAN YOU PUT A PRICE ON PEACE?BECAUSE I SURE CAN!Deadman Danny #deadlock pic.twitter.com/KJGYBhulyh September 30, 2026

Deadlock's specific emphasis on New Yorkian archetypes also begs the question, what’s next? I need a ghostly muckraker journalist. A witch with a hot dog cart. A greedy, monstrous landlord who charges his enemies soul rent! I’m giddy for what’s to come the same way I am with a crossover fighting game, but there’s not that latent stench of knowing it all doubles as advertising for other products. For every bit it’s a pulpy fantasy world, Deadlock is a celebration of the real one outside. And where other MOBAs are sketching in familiar margins, it still feels fresh two years into its "private" playtest.

items.title: 你的生活有没有被你在 MMO 中遇到的人改变过？
items.summary: Raise a glass to your digital ride-or-dies.

content.v: https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/PgGhmt5pTtxusaQQX3dHPF-1920-80.png

This is Terminally Online : PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about their MMO of choice.

WoW: Forever's had me nostalgic for a bygone era of MMOs that seems to be enjoying a touch of a resurgence—the idea of a lived-in immersive world, versus the daily task theme park of modern MMO design. Not that I have anything against the latter, mind. Theme parks are neat and roller coasters are fun.

But I have, true to the point, been grouping up with strangers more often in a slower-burn world, partially for convenience, but also partially because the slower pace has me less hungry for rampant progress and time saving. I've gotta hike for six minutes to get to this quest anyway, why wouldn't I stop and help someone in trouble?

When I get all sappy and soft-hearted like this, I also think of The Remarkable Life of Ibelin , a documentary about a WoW player Mats Steen, who sadly died in 2014 of Duchenne muscular dystrophy—a man whose closest online friends travelled from across the world to attend his funeral.

Steen had a massive impact that I wouldn't presume to match, but in my 16 years playing MMOs (and roleplaying in them, like some kind of nerd), I've also met a lot of people who have changed my life. My first girlfriend, for instance—but I've also made a lot of friends who've become part of my social makeup, as much as any of my "real" pals.

I won't name them for privacy's sake, but one of these people—though I've only heard their voice for the better half of a decade we've known each other, for reasons I cannot share—has been a constant force of good in my life, and I hers. We've pulled each other out of some real mental swamps in the time we've known each other, and I've even met her sister in the real world through sheer accident.

Hopping from City of Heroes: Homecoming to Final Fantasy 14, we've told countless stories together in both MMOs. We know plenty about each other—she knows I write for this very website—but it's all been in the tiny, cosy window of Discord. It would not be going too far to call this person one of my best friends, and while I have a more regular balance of "real world" mates and digital friendships, the latter ones have never stopped being vital.

Ultimately, the friendships are what make these games—beyond any trick of design, art asset, raid, or loot system—special. As such, I'm carving out this week's Terminally Online to ask you all about the folks you've met in MMOs who've changed your life for the better: Please share in the comments below!
